citation: Horni, A., Nagel, K., Axhausen, K.W. (eds.) (2016). The Multi-Agent Transport Simulation MATSim. London: Ubiquity Press. doi:10.5334/baw (CC-BY 4.0)
description: MATSim is an open-source Java framework for large-scale agent-based transport simulation. Its toolbox of modules, which can be combined or replaced, covers demand modelling, an agent-based mobility simulation of traffic flow on road and public transport networks, re-planning of agents' daily plans, a controller that iterates simulations until behaviour settles, and output analysis; whole days are simulated second by second for car, transit, walking, cycling and demand-responsive modes. Community-maintained contribs add accessibility, bicycle, carsharing, demand-responsive transport, electric vehicles, emissions, freight, noise, parking, road pricing, signals, shared mobility, rail operation (railsim) and calibration (cadyts). It is developed by the MATSim contributors and the MATSim Association on GitHub as matsim-org, with TU Berlin's VSP group among the core developers, and released under the GNU General Public License version 2 or later at no cost. Annual releases (2024.0, 2025.0, 2026.0 on 10 April 2026) are complemented by weekly and pull-request builds on the MATSim Maven repository; official Python tools are on PyPI. The framework is location independent: scenarios for any city or country are built from a network, a synthetic population with daily plans and optionally a transit schedule; operators such as Swiss Federal Railways run national models. Caveats: building and calibrating a scenario is a substantial effort, contribs are maintained by individual community members without guarantees, and the reference book dates from 2016, updated only in yearly user-guide chapters. Simulation uses are agent-based simulation, network flow, capacity planning and emergency response, including evacuation planning described in the MATSim book. No other catalogued records relate directly yet.

Release 2026.0 is confirmed by its git tag (2026-04-10). The website's search does not work for scripts, so evacuation was checked through the literature.
